title: Buy Berlin Tickets on Your Phone - Quick Summary
items: **Yes, every Berlin ticket sells on your phone.** There are no ticket gates in Berlin, so a ticket in an app works exactly like a paper one. Singles, day tickets, the group day ticket, the airport ABC ticket and the Deutschlandticket are all available digitally, and it is usually faster than the machine.

**One app is enough: start with BVG Fahrinfo.** It plans your route and sells the right ticket at the end of it. **BVG Tickets** is a faster buy-only app, **Jelbi** adds scooters and bikes, and **VBB Bus & Bahn** or **DB Navigator** are best for Potsdam and BER regional trains.

**Know which ticket to tap (2026 fares).** Single AB **€4.00**, short-trip Kurzstrecke **€2.80**, 24-hour AB **€11.20**, 24-hour group up to 5 people **€35.30**, Deutschlandticket **€63/month**. The day ticket pays off from about the third ride.

**Zone AB covers the whole city; add zone C only for BER Airport or Potsdam.** For those, buy the **ABC** version: single €5.00 or 24-hour €12.90. Buying the wrong zone is the most common phone-ticket mistake.

**A phone ticket does not need stamping.** The yellow and red boxes are for paper tickets. A mobile ticket is valid the moment you buy it, so you just board. A screenshot is not valid: keep the live ticket open in the app for the inspector.

**You do not need a German bank account.** Pay by card, PayPal, Apple Pay or Google Pay, and buy singles and day tickets as a guest. Buy on the platform before you board, because your signal drops in the tunnel and the fine for no ticket is €60.
